1	# TimeVault
2	
3	TimeVault is a small bitemporal entity store. Every attribute value it holds is
4	stamped on two independent time axes:
5	
6	- **valid time** — when the fact was true in the business world
7	  (`valid_from` inclusive, `valid_end` exclusive);
8	- **transaction time** — when the system came to know the fact (`recorded_at`).
9	
10	A correction never overwrites history. It appends a new version, truncates the
11	valid window of the value it supersedes, and leaves that earlier value readable
12	in the history forever. Reads take one instant on each axis (`as_of` and
13	`known_at`), which is what makes "what did we believe on Tuesday about last
14	March?" answerable.
15	
16	## Requirements
17	
18	- Python 3.11 or newer
19	- no third-party runtime dependencies
20	
21	## Run the service
22	
23	```bash
24	PYTHONPATH=src python -m timevault.server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --database timevault.db
25	```
26	
27	The process prints `TimeVault listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080` after it has
28	bound the port.
29	
30	## The two axes
31	
32	| axis | written by | read by | interval |
33	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
34	| valid time | `valid_from` / `valid_end` of a fact | `as_of` | `[from, end)` |
35	| transaction time | the injected clock, one instant per write | `known_at` | `[recorded_at, superseded_at)` here, `[recorded_at, now)` if still current |
36	
37	Both coordinates of the transaction interval are transaction instants: `recorded_at`
38	is when the write was recorded and `superseded_at` is when a later write stopped
39	the version being current. Neither is ever a business instant, so the interval can
40	never run backwards. `superseded_at` is `null` while the version is still current.
41	
42	Both axes accept an RFC 3339 instant such as `2024-05-31T00:00:00Z`, an integer
43	count of milliseconds since the Unix epoch, or a float count of seconds since
44	the epoch. Internally every coordinate is an integer millisecond count, so
45	ordering and equality are exact. A `GET` with no query projects at the current
46	instant on both axes.
47	
48	`known_at` is a cutoff: a version recorded after it does not exist for that read,
49	so a window that a later correction truncated still looks open ended at that
50	earlier transaction time.
51	
52	## Data model
53	
54	An entity is a set of named attributes under a `type` and an `id`. Values must
55	be a string, a number, a boolean, or `null`; objects and arrays are rejected.
56	The ledger keeps one row per **attribute version**:
57	
58	| field | axis | meaning |
59	| --- | --- | --- |
60	| `version` | — | per-attribute counter, from 1, never reused |
61	| `operation` | — | `assert` (holds `value`) or `retract` (holds nothing) |
62	| `value` | — | the asserted value, `null` for a retraction |
63	| `valid_from` | valid | inclusive start of the valid window |
64	| `declared_end` | valid | the exclusive end the assertion declared, `null` if it declared none; never moves |
65	| `valid_end` | valid | exclusive end of the window once every correction so far has applied its trim, `null` while open ended |
66	| `recorded_at` | transaction | when the write request was recorded |
67	| `superseded_at` | transaction | when a later write stopped this version being current, `null` while current |
68	
69	`declared_end` and `valid_end` differ exactly when a correction pulled the window
70	back: the declared bound is what the row was written with, the effective bound is
71	where the last trim of that window left it. The two together are what let a
72	reader before the trim see the open ended window the row actually had. A single
73	window can be trimmed more than once, by a correction in force and then by a
74	backdated restatement that lands earlier still; each trim appends its own
75	`truncations` row, so a reader between two trims sees the end the first one left
76	and never the earlier end the second one pulled it back to.
77	
78	Rows are append-only. A correction appends its own row, and the only columns it
79	ever updates on an older row are `valid_end` and `declared_end` — that update is
80	the trim. Every trim is also appended to the `truncations` table, one row per
81	event, stamped with the trim's **transaction instant**:
82	`(type, id, attribute, version, recorded_at, valid_end)`. A trim is knowledge, so
83	the truncation carries the instant it was learned; a per-version stamp instead of
84	one row per event could not describe a window trimmed twice, because the second
85	trim would overwrite the first one's instant.
86	
87	### How a write lands
88	
89	`PUT /entities/{type}/{id}` takes `as_of` (the correction's effective instant,
90	default *now*) and a non-empty `facts` array. A fact is
91	`{attribute, value, valid_from?, valid_end?, deleted?}` and is placed at its own
92	`valid_from`, which defaults to the correction's `as_of`. For the attribute a
93	fact touches:
94	
95	1. every version whose `valid_from` is at or after the landing point is
96	   superseded — it keeps its value and its own `valid_end` bound, but no `as_of`
97	   selects it, because a newer version took over where it began; the trim is
98	   recorded with the transaction instant of this write;
99	2. the version straddling the landing point keeps its value and only has its
100	   `valid_end` pulled back to the landing point, so the new value replaces it
101	   from then on;
102	3. the fact is appended: an `assert` holding the given value and an optional
103	   declared `valid_end`, or a `retract` with an empty window at the landing
104	   point when `deleted` is `true`.
105	
106	A fact at or after the correction's effective instant takes effect immediately,
107	so the value it displaced stops there. A fact that declares its own earlier
108	`valid_from` is a **backdated restatement**: it is placed at that instant and
109	takes over the valid time from there, which cuts the window of the value it
110	displaced and usually leaves that value holding only the part of its own window
111	that nothing newer claimed. A restatement never rewrites the interval between its
112	own instant and the correction's, and the flat result is always a set of
113	non-overlapping windows: each version holds valid time from its `valid_from`
114	until the next version (in valid time) begins, its own declared `valid_end`, or
115	the `valid_end` its trims left it, whichever comes first.
116	
117	A retraction is a row with an empty valid window at the instant the attribute
118	ceased to exist. It is never selectable by `as_of`; it exists so the window
119	before it has a boundary and so the history records that the attribute was
120	withdrawn rather than corrected. The value it withdrew keeps its own
121	`valid_end`, so that window still looks open ended for a `known_at` earlier than
122	the retraction was recorded.
123	
124	### How a read projects
125	
126	For one attribute and a reader's `known_at`:
127	
128	1. discard every version recorded after `known_at`, and every trim recorded
129	   after it — the reader could not see either;
130	2. a remaining version holds valid time from its `valid_from` until the earliest
131	   of: the `valid_from` of the next version the reader can see, its declared
132	   `valid_end`, and the instant a trim the reader can see pulled its window back;
133	3. a version whose only truncation was written after `known_at` keeps an open
134	   ended window for that reader, because at that instant nobody had written the
135	   bound. No stored `valid_end` leaks backwards past the write that put it there;
136	4. a retraction row always holds an empty window, and it closes the window in
137	   front of it only from the instant it was recorded onwards;
138	5. `as_of` selects the newest version whose half-open window contains it. If no
139	   attribute is in effect, that attribute is absent from the response, and an
140	   entity with nothing in effect at that instant is `not_found`.
141	
142	Step 3 is what makes the upper axis exact.
143	
144	#### Worked example for step 3
145	
146	Three instants, one entity, one correction:
147	
148	| event | transaction instant | what it writes |
149	| --- | --- | --- |
150	| W1 | `2026-10-02T06:30:16.984Z` | `tier = gold`, valid from `2024-01-01`, open ended |
151	| W2 | `2026-10-02T06:30:16.987Z` | `tier = platinum`, effective `2024-03-01`; trims gold to end at `2024-03-01` |
152	
153	Reading `GET /entities/account/acct-1?as_of=2024-04-01T00:00:00Z` at three
154	`known_at` values, the answer follows by hand from rule 2 and rule 3:
155	
156	| `known_at` | versions visible | trims visible | gold's window | window at `2024-04-01` contains it? | answer |
157	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
158	| `06:30:16.985Z` | gold | none | `[2024-01-01, ∞)` | yes | `gold` |
159	| `06:30:16.986Z` | gold | none | `[2024-01-01, ∞)` | yes | `gold` |
160	| `06:30:16.987Z` | gold, platinum | gold ends `2024-03-01` | `[2024-01-01, 2024-03-01)` | no | `platinum` |
161	
162	The first two rows are rule 3: W2's trim is recorded at `.987Z`, so at `.985Z`
163	and `.986Z` the trim does not exist yet and gold still runs to `[2024-01-01, ∞)`.
164	In the last row the reader is at W2's own instant, so it sees both the trim that
165	ends gold at `2024-03-01` and the platinum version that takes over there;
166	`2024-04-01` falls in platinum's window, which contains it.
167	
168	## HTTP API
169	
170	All bodies are JSON. Unknown body fields and unknown query parameters are
171	rejected with `validation_error`. Every state-changing POST and PUT requires an
172	`Idempotency-Key` header; replaying a key returns the first response and writes
173	nothing new.
174	
175	### Health
176	
177	```http
178	GET /health
179	```
180	
181	```json
182	{"status":"ok"}
183	```
184	
185	### Create an entity
186	
187	```http
188	POST /entities/account
189	Idempotency-Key: create-1
190	
191	{
192	  "id": "acct-1",
193	  "attributes": {"status": "active", "tier": "gold"},
194	  "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
195	}
196	```
197	
198	Returns HTTP 201. `valid_from` defaults to the current instant and must not be in
199	the future. Every attribute starts at version 1 with an open ended window. The
200	response is the projection at the current instant plus `created_at` — the same
201	shape as a read, and a projection carries only the fields a read reports:
202	
203	```json
204	{"type": "account", "id": "acct-1",
205	 "as_of": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z", "known_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z",
206	 "created_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z",
207	 "attributes": {
208	   "status": {"value": "active", "version": 1, "operation": "assert",
209	              "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z", "valid_end": null,
210	              "declared_end": null,
211	              "recorded_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z"},
212	   "tier": {"value": "gold", "version": 1, "operation": "assert",
213	            "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z", "valid_end": null,
214	            "declared_end": null,
215	            "recorded_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z"}}}
216	```
217	
218	Creating the same `type`/`id` again is `conflict` (409).
219	
220	### Correct an entity
221	
222	```http
223	PUT /entities/account/acct-1
224	Idempotency-Key: fix-1
225	
226	{
227	  "as_of": "2024-03-01T00:00:00Z",
228	  "facts": [
229	    {"attribute": "tier", "value": "platinum"},
230	    {"attribute": "region", "value": "emea"},
231	    {"attribute": "status", "deleted": true}
232	  ]
233	}
234	```
235	
236	Returns HTTP 200 with the projection at the current instant, so the response
237	always shows the entity as it is now believed to be; a write is never a 404, even
238	if the correction leaves nothing in effect right now. Afterwards `tier` holds
239	`platinum` and `region` exists from 2024-03-01, `status` holds nothing from
240	2024-03-01, and the earlier `tier` and `status` values remain readable through
241	`as_of` before 2024-03-01 and through `/history`.
242	
243	A fact that would create an empty window (for example a `valid_end` at or before
244	the window start) is a `validation_error`, because a version's window is never
245	made empty by an ordinary correction.
246	
247	### Read an entity
248	
249	```http
250	GET /entities/account/acct-1?as_of=2024-02-01T00:00:00Z
251	GET /entities/account/acct-1?as_of=2024-02-01T00:00:00Z&known_at=2024-05-15T00:00:00Z
252	GET /entities/account/acct-1
253	```
254	
255	```json
256	{"type": "account", "id": "acct-1",
257	 "as_of": "2024-02-01T00:00:00.000Z", "known_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z",
258	 "attributes": {
259	   "status": {"value": "active", "version": 1, "operation": "assert",
260	              "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
261	              "valid_end": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z",
262	              "recorded_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z"},
263	   "tier": {"value": "gold", "version": 1, "operation": "assert",
264	            "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
265	            "valid_end": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z",
266	            "recorded_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z"}}}
267	```
268	
269	Both parameters default to the current instant. `valid_end` in a response is the
270	window as it appears to that reader, so it reflects the trims recorded up to
271	`known_at` and nothing later. An instant before the entity's first valid
272	time, one where no attribute is in effect, or a `known_at` earlier than the
273	entity was recorded, is `not_found`.
274	
275	### Read the history
276	
277	```http
278	GET /entities/account/acct-1/history
279	GET /entities/account/acct-1/history?known_at=2024-05-15T00:00:00Z
280	```
281	
282	Every version of every attribute, ordered by valid time, with the window as it
283	stands in the ledger for that reader:
284	
285	```json
286	{"type": "account", "id": "acct-1",
287	 "created_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z", "known_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z",
288	 "attributes": [{"attribute": "tier", "versions": [
289	   {"attribute": "tier", "version": 1, "operation": "assert", "value": "gold",
290	    "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z", "valid_from_ms": 1704067200000,
291	    "valid_end": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z", "valid_end_ms": 1709251200000,
292	    "declared_end": null,
293	    "recorded_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z",
294	    "superseded_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z"},
295	   {"attribute": "tier", "version": 2, "operation": "assert", "value": "platinum",
296	    "valid_from": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z", "valid_from_ms": 1709251200000,
297	    "valid_end": null, "valid_end_ms": null, "declared_end": null,
298	    "recorded_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z", "superseded_at": null}]}]}
299	```
300	
301	`superseded_at` is the transaction instant a later write stopped the version
302	being current, and it is `null` while the version is still current. It is not the
303	business instant the window ended at: that is `valid_end`, and for version 1 the
304	two are different instants, `2024-03-01` against `2024-05-31`. Gold was written
305	on `2024-05-01` (`recorded_at`) and superseded on `2024-05-31` (`superseded_at`),
306	so its transaction interval is `[2024-05-01, 2024-05-31)` — it can never be
307	inverted, whatever the effective instant of the correction was.
308	
309	`declared_end` is the bound the assertion itself declared, `null` here because
310	gold declared none; `valid_end` is where the correction trimmed it. `recorded_at`
311	filters out versions recorded after the reader's instant, and the same cutoff
312	hides the trims recorded after it, so a correction recorded after `known_at`
313	disappears from that earlier history view and the window it trimmed reads as open
314	ended there.
315	
316	### Diff two business instants
317	
318	```http
319	GET /diff?type=account&id=acct-1&from=2024-02-01T00:00:00Z&to=2024-04-01T00:00:00Z
320	GET /diff?type=account&id=acct-1&from=...&to=...&known_at=2024-05-15T00:00:00Z&attribute=tier
321	```
322	
323	Compares the two projections under one knowledge cutoff (the current instant
324	unless `known_at` is given) and reports one entry per attribute whose value
325	differs:
326	
327	```json
328	{"type": "account", "id": "acct-1",
329	 "from": "2024-02-01T00:00:00.000Z", "to": "2024-04-01T00:00:00.000Z",
330	 "known_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z",
331	 "changes": [
332	   {"attribute": "region", "change": "added", "before": null,
333	    "after": {"value": "emea", "version": 1, "operation": "assert",
334	              "valid_from": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z", "valid_end": null,
335	              "recorded_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z"}},
336	   {"attribute": "status", "change": "removed",
337	    "before": {"value": "active", "version": 1, "operation": "assert",
338	               "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
339	               "valid_end": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z",
340	               "recorded_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z"},
341	    "after": null}]}
342	```
343	
344	`change` is `added` when the attribute holds nothing at `from` and something at
345	`to`, `removed` for the reverse, and `changed` when both hold a different value.
346	An attribute whose value carried across the interval is not a change, even if a
347	different version supplies it. `attribute` may be repeated to narrow the result;
348	naming an attribute the entity never had is a `validation_error`. `to` must be
349	strictly later than `from`, and the entity must be in effect at both instants.
350	
351	## Errors
352	
353	```json
354	{"error":{"code":"validation_error","message":"human readable detail"}}
355	```
356	
357	Validation errors return 400, unknown routes and entities that are not in effect
358	at the requested instant return 404, and a duplicate entity, a reused
359	idempotency key, or a correction that would predate the entity returns 409.
360	
361	## Invariants
362	
363	- The ledger is append-only; a correction only ever moves a `valid_end` earlier
364	  and never deletes a value.
365	- Valid windows of one attribute never overlap.
366	- The same `(as_of, known_at)` pair always yields the same projection.
367	- `known_at` never exposes a correction recorded after it, and never exposes a
368	  trim recorded after it either.
369	- A transaction interval never runs backwards: `superseded_at` is a transaction
370	  instant at or after `recorded_at`, never a business instant.
371	- A version never has `valid_end` before `valid_from`, and a window that a
372	  correction made empty stays in the history carrying
373	  `valid_end == valid_from`. The empty window of a retraction row is
374	  intentional, not an overlap.
375	
376	## Tests
377	
378	```bash
379	PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
380	```

- **transaction time** — when the system came to know the fact (`recorded_at`).

A correction never overwrites history. It appends a new version, truncates the
valid window of the value it supersedes, and leaves that earlier value readable
in the history forever. Reads take one instant on each axis (`as_of` and
`known_at`), which is what makes "what did we believe on Tuesday about last
March?" answerable.

## Requirements

- Python 3.11 or newer
- no third-party runtime dependencies

## Run the service

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m timevault.server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --database timevault.db
```

The process prints `TimeVault listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080` after it has
bound the port.

## The two axes

| axis | written by | read by | interval |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| valid time | `valid_from` / `valid_end` of a fact | `as_of` | `[from, end)` |
| transaction time | the injected clock, one instant per write | `known_at` | `[recorded_at, superseded_at)` here, `[recorded_at, now)` if still current |

Both coordinates of the transaction interval are transaction instants: `recorded_at`
is when the write was recorded and `superseded_at` is when a later write stopped
the version being current. Neither is ever a business instant, so the interval can
never run backwards. `superseded_at` is `null` while the version is still current.

Both axes accept an RFC 3339 instant such as `2024-05-31T00:00:00Z`, an integer
count of milliseconds since the Unix epoch, or a float count of seconds since
the epoch. Internally every coordinate is an integer millisecond count, so
ordering and equality are exact. A `GET` with no query projects at the current
instant on both axes.

`known_at` is a cutoff: a version recorded after it does not exist for that read,
so a window that a later correction truncated still looks open ended at that
earlier transaction time.

## Data model

An entity is a set of named attributes under a `type` and an `id`. Values must
be a string, a number, a boolean, or `null`; objects and arrays are rejected.
The ledger keeps one row per **attribute version**:

| field | axis | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | — | per-attribute counter, from 1, never reused |
| `operation` | — | `assert` (holds `value`) or `retract` (holds nothing) |
| `value` | — | the asserted value, `null` for a retraction |
| `valid_from` | valid | inclusive start of the valid window |
| `declared_end` | valid | the exclusive end the assertion declared, `null` if it declared none; never moves |
| `valid_end` | valid | exclusive end of the window once every correction so far has applied its trim, `null` while open ended |
| `recorded_at` | transaction | when the write request was recorded |
| `superseded_at` | transaction | when a later write stopped this version being current, `null` while current |

`declared_end` and `valid_end` differ exactly when a correction pulled the window
back: the declared bound is what the row was written with, the effective bound is
where the last trim of that window left it. The two together are what let a
reader before the trim see the open ended window the row actually had. A single
window can be trimmed more than once, by a correction in force and then by a
backdated restatement that lands earlier still; each trim appends its own
`truncations` row, so a reader between two trims sees the end the first one left
and never the earlier end the second one pulled it back to.

Rows are append-only. A correction appends its own row, and the only columns it
ever updates on an older row are `valid_end` and `declared_end` — that update is
the trim. Every trim is also appended to the `truncations` table, one row per
event, stamped with the trim's **transaction instant**:
`(type, id, attribute, version, recorded_at, valid_end)`. A trim is knowledge, so
the truncation carries the instant it was learned; a per-version stamp instead of
one row per event could not describe a window trimmed twice, because the second
trim would overwrite the first one's instant.

### How a write lands

`PUT /entities/{type}/{id}` takes `as_of` (the correction's effective instant,
default *now*) and a non-empty `facts` array. A fact is
`{attribute, value, valid_from?, valid_end?, deleted?}` and is placed at its own
`valid_from`, which defaults to the correction's `as_of`. For the attribute a
fact touches:

1. every version whose `valid_from` is at or after the landing point is
   superseded — it keeps its value and its own `valid_end` bound, but no `as_of`
   selects it, because a newer version took over where it began; the trim is
   recorded with the transaction instant of this write;
2. the version straddling the landing point keeps its value and only has its
   `valid_end` pulled back to the landing point, so the new value replaces it
   from then on;
3. the fact is appended: an `assert` holding the given value and an optional
   declared `valid_end`, or a `retract` with an empty window at the landing
   point when `deleted` is `true`.

A fact at or after the correction's effective instant takes effect immediately,
so the value it displaced stops there. A fact that declares its own earlier
`valid_from` is a **backdated restatement**: it is placed at that instant and
takes over the valid time from there, which cuts the window of the value it
displaced and usually leaves that value holding only the part of its own window
that nothing newer claimed. A restatement never rewrites the interval between its
own instant and the correction's, and the flat result is always a set of
non-overlapping windows: each version holds valid time from its `valid_from`
until the next version (in valid time) begins, its own declared `valid_end`, or
the `valid_end` its trims left it, whichever comes first.

A retraction is a row with an empty valid window at the instant the attribute
ceased to exist. It is never selectable by `as_of`; it exists so the window
before it has a boundary and so the history records that the attribute was
withdrawn rather than corrected. The value it withdrew keeps its own
`valid_end`, so that window still looks open ended for a `known_at` earlier than
the retraction was recorded.

### How a read projects

For one attribute and a reader's `known_at`:

1. discard every version recorded after `known_at`, and every trim recorded
   after it — the reader could not see either;
2. a remaining version holds valid time from its `valid_from` until the earliest
   of: the `valid_from` of the next version the reader can see, its declared
   `valid_end`, and the instant a trim the reader can see pulled its window back;
3. a version whose only truncation was written after `known_at` keeps an open
   ended window for that reader, because at that instant nobody had written the
   bound. No stored `valid_end` leaks backwards past the write that put it there;
4. a retraction row always holds an empty window, and it closes the window in
   front of it only from the instant it was recorded onwards;
5. `as_of` selects the newest version whose half-open window contains it. If no
   attribute is in effect, that attribute is absent from the response, and an
   entity with nothing in effect at that instant is `not_found`.

Step 3 is what makes the upper axis exact.

#### Worked example for step 3

Three instants, one entity, one correction:

| event | transaction instant | what it writes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| W1 | `2026-10-02T06:30:16.984Z` | `tier = gold`, valid from `2024-01-01`, open ended |
| W2 | `2026-10-02T06:30:16.987Z` | `tier = platinum`, effective `2024-03-01`; trims gold to end at `2024-03-01` |

Reading `GET /entities/account/acct-1?as_of=2024-04-01T00:00:00Z` at three
`known_at` values, the answer follows by hand from rule 2 and rule 3:

| `known_at` | versions visible | trims visible | gold's window | window at `2024-04-01` contains it? | answer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `06:30:16.985Z` | gold | none | `[2024-01-01, ∞)` | yes | `gold` |
| `06:30:16.986Z` | gold | none | `[2024-01-01, ∞)` | yes | `gold` |
| `06:30:16.987Z` | gold, platinum | gold ends `2024-03-01` | `[2024-01-01, 2024-03-01)` | no | `platinum` |

The first two rows are rule 3: W2's trim is recorded at `.987Z`, so at `.985Z`
and `.986Z` the trim does not exist yet and gold still runs to `[2024-01-01, ∞)`.
In the last row the reader is at W2's own instant, so it sees both the trim that
ends gold at `2024-03-01` and the platinum version that takes over there;
`2024-04-01` falls in platinum's window, which contains it.

## HTTP API

All bodies are JSON. Unknown body fields and unknown query parameters are
rejected with `validation_error`. Every state-changing POST and PUT requires an
`Idempotency-Key` header; replaying a key returns the first response and writes
nothing new.

### Health

```http
GET /health
```

```json
{"status":"ok"}
```

### Create an entity

```http
POST /entities/account
Idempotency-Key: create-1

{
  "id": "acct-1",
  "attributes": {"status": "active", "tier": "gold"},
  "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

Returns HTTP 201. `valid_from` defaults to the current instant and must not be in
the future. Every attribute starts at version 1 with an open ended window. The
response is the projection at the current instant plus `created_at` — the same
shape as a read, and a projection carries only the fields a read reports:

```json
{"type": "account", "id": "acct-1",
 "as_of": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z", "known_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z",
 "created_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z",
 "attributes": {
   "status": {"value": "active", "version": 1, "operation": "assert",
              "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z", "valid_end": null,
              "declared_end": null,
              "recorded_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z"},
   "tier": {"value": "gold", "version": 1, "operation": "assert",
            "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z", "valid_end": null,
            "declared_end": null,
            "recorded_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z"}}}
```

Creating the same `type`/`id` again is `conflict` (409).

### Correct an entity

```http
PUT /entities/account/acct-1
Idempotency-Key: fix-1

{
  "as_of": "2024-03-01T00:00:00Z",
  "facts": [
    {"attribute": "tier", "value": "platinum"},
    {"attribute": "region", "value": "emea"},
    {"attribute": "status", "deleted": true}
  ]
}
```

Returns HTTP 200 with the projection at the current instant, so the response
always shows the entity as it is now believed to be; a write is never a 404, even
if the correction leaves nothing in effect right now. Afterwards `tier` holds
`platinum` and `region` exists from 2024-03-01, `status` holds nothing from
2024-03-01, and the earlier `tier` and `status` values remain readable through
`as_of` before 2024-03-01 and through `/history`.

A fact that would create an empty window (for example a `valid_end` at or before
the window start) is a `validation_error`, because a version's window is never
made empty by an ordinary correction.

### Read an entity

```http
GET /entities/account/acct-1?as_of=2024-02-01T00:00:00Z
GET /entities/account/acct-1?as_of=2024-02-01T00:00:00Z&known_at=2024-05-15T00:00:00Z
GET /entities/account/acct-1
```

```json
{"type": "account", "id": "acct-1",
 "as_of": "2024-02-01T00:00:00.000Z", "known_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z",
 "attributes": {
   "status": {"value": "active", "version": 1, "operation": "assert",
              "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
              "valid_end": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z",
              "recorded_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z"},
   "tier": {"value": "gold", "version": 1, "operation": "assert",
            "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
            "valid_end": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z",
            "recorded_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z"}}}
```

Both parameters default to the current instant. `valid_end` in a response is the
window as it appears to that reader, so it reflects the trims recorded up to
`known_at` and nothing later. An instant before the entity's first valid
time, one where no attribute is in effect, or a `known_at` earlier than the
entity was recorded, is `not_found`.

### Read the history

```http
GET /entities/account/acct-1/history
GET /entities/account/acct-1/history?known_at=2024-05-15T00:00:00Z
```

Every version of every attribute, ordered by valid time, with the window as it
stands in the ledger for that reader:

```json
{"type": "account", "id": "acct-1",
 "created_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z", "known_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z",
 "attributes": [{"attribute": "tier", "versions": [
   {"attribute": "tier", "version": 1, "operation": "assert", "value": "gold",
    "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z", "valid_from_ms": 1704067200000,
    "valid_end": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z", "valid_end_ms": 1709251200000,
    "declared_end": null,
    "recorded_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "superseded_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z"},
   {"attribute": "tier", "version": 2, "operation": "assert", "value": "platinum",
    "valid_from": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z", "valid_from_ms": 1709251200000,
    "valid_end": null, "valid_end_ms": null, "declared_end": null,
    "recorded_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z", "superseded_at": null}]}]}
```

`superseded_at` is the transaction instant a later write stopped the version
being current, and it is `null` while the version is still current. It is not the
business instant the window ended at: that is `valid_end`, and for version 1 the
two are different instants, `2024-03-01` against `2024-05-31`. Gold was written
on `2024-05-01` (`recorded_at`) and superseded on `2024-05-31` (`superseded_at`),
so its transaction interval is `[2024-05-01, 2024-05-31)` — it can never be
inverted, whatever the effective instant of the correction was.

`declared_end` is the bound the assertion itself declared, `null` here because
gold declared none; `valid_end` is where the correction trimmed it. `recorded_at`
filters out versions recorded after the reader's instant, and the same cutoff
hides the trims recorded after it, so a correction recorded after `known_at`
disappears from that earlier history view and the window it trimmed reads as open
ended there.

### Diff two business instants

```http
GET /diff?type=account&id=acct-1&from=2024-02-01T00:00:00Z&to=2024-04-01T00:00:00Z
GET /diff?type=account&id=acct-1&from=...&to=...&known_at=2024-05-15T00:00:00Z&attribute=tier
```

Compares the two projections under one knowledge cutoff (the current instant
unless `known_at` is given) and reports one entry per attribute whose value
differs:

```json
{"type": "account", "id": "acct-1",
 "from": "2024-02-01T00:00:00.000Z", "to": "2024-04-01T00:00:00.000Z",
 "known_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z",
 "changes": [
   {"attribute": "region", "change": "added", "before": null,
    "after": {"value": "emea", "version": 1, "operation": "assert",
              "valid_from": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z", "valid_end": null,
              "recorded_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z"}},
   {"attribute": "status", "change": "removed",
    "before": {"value": "active", "version": 1, "operation": "assert",
               "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
               "valid_end": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z",
               "recorded_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z"},
    "after": null}]}
```

`change` is `added` when the attribute holds nothing at `from` and something at
`to`, `removed` for the reverse, and `changed` when both hold a different value.
An attribute whose value carried across the interval is not a change, even if a
different version supplies it. `attribute` may be repeated to narrow the result;
naming an attribute the entity never had is a `validation_error`. `to` must be
strictly later than `from`, and the entity must be in effect at both instants.

## Errors

```json
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","message":"human readable detail"}}
```

Validation errors return 400, unknown routes and entities that are not in effect
at the requested instant return 404, and a duplicate entity, a reused
idempotency key, or a correction that would predate the entity returns 409.

## Invariants

- The ledger is append-only; a correction only ever moves a `valid_end` earlier
  and never deletes a value.
- Valid windows of one attribute never overlap.
- The same `(as_of, known_at)` pair always yields the same projection.
- `known_at` never exposes a correction recorded after it, and never exposes a
  trim recorded after it either.
- A transaction interval never runs backwards: `superseded_at` is a transaction
  instant at or after `recorded_at`, never a business instant.
- A version never has `valid_end` before `valid_from`, and a window that a
  correction made empty stays in the history carrying
  `valid_end == valid_from`. The empty window of a retraction row is
  intentional, not an overlap.

## Tests

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

156	    parser.add_argument("--port", default=8080, type=int)

158	    arguments = parser.parse_args()

11	@dataclass(frozen=True)
12	class Truncation:
13	    """One window-closing event, stamped on both axes.
14	
15	    ``recorded_at`` is the transaction instant the system learned the new bound,
16	    ``valid_end`` the business instant the window was closed at.
17	    """
18	
19	    version: int
20	    recorded_at: int
21	    valid_end: int

24	@dataclass(frozen=True)
25	class Version:
26	    """One stored attribute version, as read back from the database.
27	
28	    ``valid_from`` is the business instant the value starts at.  ``declared_end``
29	    is the bound the assertion itself declared and never moves; ``valid_end`` is
30	    where the window ends once every correction so far has been applied, so it is
31	    ``None`` while the window is open ended.  ``recorded_at`` is the transaction
32	    instant the row was written.
33	    """
34	
35	    attribute: str
36	    version: int
37	    operation: str
38	    value: Any
39	    valid_from: int
40	    valid_end: int | None
41	    declared_end: int | None
42	    recorded_at: int
43	    truncations: tuple[Truncation, ...] = ()
44	
45	    @classmethod
46	    def from_row(cls, row: Any) -> "Version":
47	        return cls(
48	            attribute=str(row["attribute"]),
49	            version=int(row["version"]),
50	            operation=str(row["operation"]),
51	            value=None if row["value"] is None else Store.decode(row["value"]),
52	            valid_from=int(row["valid_from"]),
53	            valid_end=None if row["valid_end"] is None else int(row["valid_end"]),
54	            declared_end=None if row["declared_end"] is None else int(row["declared_end"]),
55	            recorded_at=int(row["recorded_at"]),
56	        )

58	    def with_truncations(self, events: tuple[Truncation, ...]) -> "Version":
59	        return Version(
60	            self.attribute,
61	            self.version,
62	            self.operation,
63	            self.value,
64	            self.valid_from,
65	            self.valid_end,
66	            self.declared_end,
67	            self.recorded_at,
68	            events,

71	    def known_truncations(self, known_at: int) -> tuple[Truncation, ...]:
72	        return tuple(event for event in self.truncations if event.recorded_at <= known_at)
73	
74	    def superseded_at(self) -> int | None:
75	        """The transaction instant this version stopped being current, if it has.
76	
77	        That is the instant of a trim, never a business instant, so together with
78	        ``recorded_at`` it bounds a half-open transaction interval and can never
79	        precede it.  When several corrections closed the same window the last one
80	        is the authoritative closure, because it is the one the ledger's final
81	        ``valid_end`` comes from; the earlier trims stay in the row's truncation
82	        events, which is how a reader before a later trim still sees the end that
83	        trim had not yet moved.
84	        """
85	        return None if not self.truncations else self.truncations[-1].recorded_at
86	
87	    def end_known_at(self, known_at: int) -> int | None:
88	        """Where this version's window ended as of ``known_at``.
89	
90	        The window end is never later than the bound the assertion declared, so
91	        the answer is the earliest of that declared bound and every trim the
92	        reader already knows about.  A trim recorded after ``known_at`` is not
93	        knowledge yet, so the window it closed is still open ended — that is what
94	        keeps the upper axis exact.
95	        """
96	        end = self.declared_end
97	        for event in self.known_truncations(known_at):
98	            end = event.valid_end if end is None else min(end, event.valid_end)
99	        if end is None:
100	            return None
101	        # ``valid_end`` already folds in every trim, including ones this reader
102	        # has not learned yet, so it is only ever a safe ceiling for the end the
103	        # reader knows — never a later bound leaking backwards.
104	        return self.valid_end if self.valid_end is None else min(end, self.valid_end)
105	
106	    def as_dict(self, valid_end: Any = ...) -> dict[str, Any]:
107	        """Render the version, optionally with a recomputed window end.
108	
109	        Pass ``None`` explicitly to report an open ended window; omitting the
110	        argument reports the end as it stands in the ledger for the reader.
111	        """
112	        end = self.valid_end if valid_end is ... else valid_end
113	        declared = self.declared_end
114	        if declared is None or end is None or end >= declared:
115	            declared_field: str | None = None
116	        else:
117	            declared_field = iso(declared)
118	        return {
119	            "attribute": self.attribute,
120	            "version": self.version,
121	            "operation": self.operation,
122	            "value": self.value,
123	            "valid_from": iso(self.valid_from),
124	            "valid_from_ms": self.valid_from,
125	            "valid_end": None if end is None else iso(end),
126	            "valid_end_ms": end,
127	            "declared_end": declared_field,
128	            "recorded_at": iso(self.recorded_at),
129	            "superseded_at": None

139	def known_windows(versions: list[Version], known_at: int) -> list[Token]:
140	    """Reconstruct the valid windows of one attribute as known at ``known_at``.
141	
142	    Every version is known from its ``recorded_at`` onwards, and every truncation
143	    it carries from the ``recorded_at`` of that truncation onwards.  Working from
144	    the newest version the reader can see back to the oldest, a version holds
145	    valid time from its own ``valid_from`` until the earliest of:
146	
147	    * ``valid_from`` of the next version the reader can see, because the value
148	      written later is the one in force from then on;
149	    * the end it carries for that reader, which is its declared ``valid_end`` or,
150	      while the trim that pulled the end back is still unknown, nothing at all;
151	    * the instant a correction already known at ``known_at`` starts writing
152	      there, which is where the chain of visible corrections takes over.
153	
154	    A version whose only displacers are recorded after ``known_at`` keeps an open
155	    ended window, because at that instant nobody had written the bound — that
156	    rule is what keeps a transaction-time view exact.  Tokens come back in
157	    transaction order, oldest first.  Retraction rows always carry an empty
158	    window: they exist to mark the instant an attribute ceased to exist.
159	    """
160	    ordered = sorted(versions, key=lambda item: (item.valid_from, item.version))
161	    tokens: list[Token] = []
162	    takeover: int | None = None
163	    for index in range(len(ordered) - 1, -1, -1):
164	        version = ordered[index]
165	        if version.recorded_at > known_at:
166	            # Not recorded yet for this reader, and it could not have displaced
167	            # anything either: it is invisible to the whole pass.
168	            continue
169	        following = next(
170	            (
171	                ordered[other]
172	                for other in range(index + 1, len(ordered))
173	                if ordered[other].recorded_at <= known_at
174	            ),
175	            None,
176	        )
177	        if version.operation == "retract":
178	            # A retraction never holds valid time of its own; it only closes the
179	            # window in front of it.
180	            end: int | None = version.valid_from
181	        else:
182	            end = version.end_known_at(known_at)
183	            if following is not None:
184	                # A version the reader can see takes over where it begins.
185	                end = following.valid_from if end is None else min(end, following.valid_from)
186	            if takeover is not None:
187	                # A correction already known at ``known_at`` starts writing at
188	                # that instant, which is the end of everything before it.
189	                end = takeover if end is None else min(end, takeover)
190	        tokens.append((version, version.valid_from, end))
191	        takeover = version.valid_from
192	    tokens.sort(key=lambda token: (token[0].recorded_at, token[0].version))
193	    return tokens

196	def complete_windows(versions: list[Version], known_at: int) -> list[Token]:
197	    """The windows as they stand in the ledger, for a history listing.
198	
199	    Every version the reader can see keeps the end the ledger records for it,
200	    with any trim the reader cannot know about yet left out, so this is the
201	    full-knowledge view of the ledger for that transaction instant rather than a
202	    projection: a window a correction pulled back shows the pulled back end once
203	    that correction is knowable, and a value displaced by a backdated
204	    restatement keeps the part of its own window that no later version took over.
205	    """
206	    ordered = sorted(versions, key=lambda item: (item.valid_from, item.version))
207	    tokens: list[Token] = []
208	    for index, version in enumerate(ordered):
209	        if version.recorded_at > known_at:
210	            # Recorded after the reader's instant, so this reader never saw it.
211	            continue
212	        end = version.end_known_at(known_at)
213	        successor = next(
214	            (
215	                ordered[other]
216	                for other in range(index + 1, len(ordered))
217	                if ordered[other].recorded_at <= known_at
218	            ),
219	            None,
220	        )
221	        if successor is not None:
222	            end = successor.valid_from if end is None else min(end, successor.valid_from)
223	        tokens.append((version, version.valid_from, end))
224	    tokens.sort(key=lambda token: (token[0].valid_from, token[0].version))
225	    return tokens
226	
227	
228	def project(tokens: list[Token], at: int) -> Token | None:
229	    """Select the value that was in force at business instant ``at``.
230	
231	    Tokens arrive in transaction order, newest first.  A backdated correction can
232	    leave two windows that touch: the value it displaced keeps the window it had,
233	    and the restated value covers the earlier part of it.  The value written last
234	    is the one the ledger believes from the instant it took effect, so the
235	    newest match wins.
236	    """
237	    for token in reversed(tokens):
238	        start, end = token[1], token[2]
239	        if start <= at and (end is None or at < end):
240	            return token
241	    return None
242

244	def _value_document(entry: tuple[Any, int, str, int, int | None, int] | None) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
245	    if entry is None:
246	        return None
247	    value, version, operation, start, end, recorded_at = entry
248	    return {
249	        "value": value,
250	        "version": version,
251	        "operation": operation,
252	        "valid_from": iso(start),
253	        "valid_end": None if end is None else iso(end),
254	        "recorded_at": iso(recorded_at),
255	    }

258	class TimeVault:
259	    """Bitemporal entity store: valid time on one axis, transaction time on the other."""
260	
261	    def __init__(self, database: str, clock: Callable[[], Any] | None = None):
262	        self.store = Store(database, clock)
263	
264	    # -- writes -------------------------------------------------------------
265	
266	    def create_entity(self, entity_type: str, raw: Any, key: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
267	        moment = self.store.now()
268	        entity = Entity.parse(entity_type, raw)
269	        if "valid_from" in raw:
270	            valid_from = instant(raw["valid_from"], "valid_from")
271	            if valid_from > moment:
272	                raise ValidationError("valid_from must not be in the future")
273	        else:
274	            valid_from = moment
275	
276	        def action(recorded_at: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
277	            if self.store.entity_row(entity.type, entity.id) is not None:
278	                raise ConflictError(f"entity {entity.type}/{entity.id} already exists")
279	            self.store.insert_entity(entity.type, entity.id, recorded_at)
280	            for attribute in entity.attributes:
281	                self.store.insert_version(
282	                    entity.type,
283	                    entity.id,
284	                    attribute.name,
285	                    1,
286	                    "assert",
287	                    attribute.value,
288	                    valid_from,
289	                    None,
290	                    recorded_at,
291	                )
292	            document = self._read(entity.type, entity.id, recorded_at, recorded_at)
293	            document["created_at"] = iso(recorded_at)
294	            return document
295	
296	        return self._idempotent(key, f"create:{entity.type}/{entity.id}", action, moment)
297	
298	    def apply_correction(
299	        self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str, raw: Any, key: str | None
300	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
301	        now = self.store.now()
302	        correction = Correction.parse(raw, now)
303	
304	        def action(recorded_at: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
305	            row = self.store.entity_row(entity_type, entity_id)
306	            if row is None:
307	                raise NotFoundError(f"entity {entity_type}/{entity_id} does not exist")
308	            if int(row["created_at"]) > recorded_at:
309	                raise ConflictError(
310	                    f"cannot state a fact about {entity_type}/{entity_id} before it existed"
311	                )
312	            for fact in correction.facts:
313	                self._apply_fact(entity_type, entity_id, fact, recorded_at)
314	            # ``as_of`` equal to the instant just recorded means "every window
315	            # that starts when this fact takes effect", which describes the
316	            # attribute as it stands after the correction rather than the state
317	            # that the correction replaced.  A write is never a 404, so an
318	            # entity with nothing in effect right now answers with no attributes.
319	            return self._read(entity_type, entity_id, recorded_at, recorded_at, required=False)
320	
321	        return self._idempotent(key, f"correct:{entity_type}/{entity_id}", action, now)
322	
323	    # -- reads --------------------------------------------------------------
324	
325	    def entity_as_of(
326	        self,
327	        entity_type: str,
328	        entity_id: str,
329	        as_of: Any = None,
330	        known_at: Any = None,
331	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
332	        """Project the entity onto a business instant and a knowledge instant.
333	
334	        Both axes default to the current instant, so a plain GET returns the
335	        entity as it is believed to be right now.  Each argument accepts an RFC
336	        3339 string or an integer count of epoch milliseconds.
337	        """
338	        moment = self.store.now()
339	        return self._read(
340	            entity_type,
341	            entity_id,
342	            moment if as_of is None else instant(as_of, "as_of"),
343	            moment if known_at is None else instant(known_at, "known_at"),
344	        )
345	
346	    def history(
347	        self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str, known_at: Any = None
348	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
349	        row = self.store.entity_row(entity_type, entity_id)
350	        if row is None:
351	            raise NotFoundError(f"entity {entity_type}/{entity_id} does not exist")
352	        if known_at is None:
353	            known_at = self.store.now()
354	        else:
355	            known_at = instant(known_at, "known_at")
356	        grouped = self._grouped_versions(entity_type, entity_id)
357	        attributes = []
358	        for name in sorted(grouped):
359	            tokens = complete_windows(grouped[name], known_at)
360	            attributes.append(
361	                {
362	                    "attribute": name,
363	                    "versions": [
364	                        version.as_dict(valid_end) for version, _, valid_end in tokens
365	                    ],
366	                }
367	            )
368	        return {
369	            "type": entity_type,
370	            "id": entity_id,
371	            "created_at": iso(int(row["created_at"])),
372	            "known_at": iso(known_at),
373	            "attributes": attributes,
374	        }
375	
376	    def diff(
377	        self,
378	        entity_type: str,
379	        entity_id: str,
380	        start: Any,
381	        end: Any,
382	        known_at: Any = None,
383	        names: list[str] | None = None,
384	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
385	        start = instant(start, "from")
386	        end = instant(end, "to")
387	        known_at = self.store.now() if known_at is None else instant(known_at, "known_at")
388	        if end <= start:
389	            raise ValidationError("to must be strictly later than from")
390	        if names is not None and len(set(names)) != len(names):
391	            raise ValidationError("attribute may not be repeated")
392	        left = self._projection(entity_type, entity_id, start, known_at)
393	        right = self._projection(entity_type, entity_id, end, known_at)
394	        selected = sorted(set(left) | set(right))
395	        if names is not None:
396	            wanted = set(names)
397	            unknown = sorted(wanted - set(self._all_attributes(entity_type, entity_id)))
398	            if unknown:
399	                raise ValidationError(f"unknown attribute(s): {', '.join(unknown)}")
400	            selected = [name for name in selected if name in wanted]
401	
402	        changes = []
403	        for name in selected:
404	            before = left.get(name)
405	            after = right.get(name)
406	            if before is None and after is None:
407	                continue
408	            if before is not None and after is not None and value_same(before[0], after[0]):
409	                # The value carried across the boundary; only the version that
410	                # supplies it changed, which is not a business-time difference.
411	                continue
412	            if before is None:
413	                kind = "added"
414	            elif after is None:
415	                kind = "removed"
416	            else:
417	                kind = "changed"
418	            changes.append(
419	                {
420	                    "attribute": name,
421	                    "change": kind,
422	                    "before": _value_document(before),
423	                    "after": _value_document(after),
424	                }
425	            )
426	        return {
427	            "type": entity_type,
428	            "id": entity_id,
429	            "from": iso(start),
430	            "to": iso(end),
431	            "known_at": iso(known_at),
432	            "changes": changes,
433	        }
434	
435	    # -- internals ----------------------------------------------------------
436	
437	    def _idempotent(
438	        self,
439	        key: str | None,
440	        operation: str,
441	        action: Callable[[int], dict[str, Any]],
442	        moment: int,
443	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
444	        """Run ``action`` once per ``key`` and remember the first response.
445	
446	        The whole check-and-write happens in one immediate transaction so two
447	        concurrent deliveries of the same key cannot both run the action.
448	        """
449	        if not key:
450	            raise ValidationError("Idempotency-Key header is required")
451	        with self.store.transaction() as connection:
452	            remembered = self.store.remembered_operation(key)
453	            if remembered is not None:
454	                if remembered != operation:
455	                    raise ConflictError(
456	                        "idempotency key was already used for another operation"
457	                    )
458	                row = connection.execute(
459	                    "SELECT response FROM idempotency WHERE key = ?", (key,)
460	                ).fetchone()
461	                return Store.decode(row["response"])
462	            response = action(moment)
463	            self.store.remember(key, operation, response)
464	            return response
465	
466	    def _apply_fact(self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str, fact: Fact, recorded_at: int) -> None:
467	        """Place one fact on the ledger.
468	
469	        The fact lands at ``fact.valid_from``.  It takes effect in the ledger at
470	        that same instant, or at ``recorded_at`` when the fact is backdated: a
471	        backdated correction is placed in the past but only displaces the tail
472	        it supersedes, it does not restate the time between its own effective
473	        instant and the correction's effective instant.
474	        """
475	        effective = max(fact.valid_from or recorded_at, recorded_at)
476	        # A retraction needs no truncation pass: its own row sits after every
477	        # version recorded before it and bounds the window in front of it.
478	        if not fact.deleted:
479	            self.store.truncate_attribute(
480	                entity_type, entity_id, fact.attribute, fact.valid_from, effective, recorded_at
481	            )
482	        self.store.insert_version(
483	            entity_type,
484	            entity_id,
485	            fact.attribute,
486	            self.store.next_version(entity_type, entity_id, fact.attribute),
487	            fact.operation,
488	            fact.value,
489	            fact.valid_from,
490	            # A retraction is stored as an empty window at the instant the
491	            # attribute ceased to exist.  It is never selectable by as_of; it
492	            # exists so the window before it has a boundary and so the history
493	            # records that the attribute was withdrawn rather than corrected.
494	            fact.valid_from if fact.deleted else fact.valid_end,
495	            recorded_at,
496	        )
497	
498	    def _grouped_versions(self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str) -> dict[str, list[Version]]:
499	        """Every version of the entity, with the trims it took attached.
500	
501	        A trim lives in its own append-only row, so one version can carry several
502	        — one per correction that closed its window.  They are loaded once here
503	        and attached by version number, which is what lets a projection drop the
504	        trims the reader cannot know about yet.
505	        """
506	        events: dict[str, dict[int, list[Truncation]]] = {}
507	        for row in self.store.truncations_for_entity(entity_type, entity_id):
508	            version = int(row["version"])
509	            by_version = events.setdefault(str(row["attribute"]), {})
510	            by_version.setdefault(version, []).append(
511	                Truncation(
512	                    version=version,
513	                    recorded_at=int(row["recorded_at"]),
514	                    valid_end=int(row["valid_end"]),
515	                )
516	            )
517	        grouped: dict[str, list[Version]] = {}
518	        for row in self.store.versions_for_entity(entity_type, entity_id):
519	            version = Version.from_row(row)
520	            attached = events.get(version.attribute, {}).get(version.version, [])
521	            grouped.setdefault(version.attribute, []).append(
522	                version.with_truncations(tuple(attached))
523	            )
524	        return grouped
525	
526	    def _all_attributes(self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str) -> set[str]:
527	        return set(self._grouped_versions(entity_type, entity_id))
528	
529	    def _read(
530	        self,
531	        entity_type: str,
532	        entity_id: str,
533	        as_of: int,
534	        known_at: int,
535	        required: bool = True,
536	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
537	        projection = self._projection(entity_type, entity_id, as_of, known_at, required)
538	        attributes = {
539	            name: {
540	                "value": entry[0],
541	                "version": entry[1],
542	                "operation": entry[2],
543	                "valid_from": iso(entry[3]),
544	                "valid_end": None if entry[4] is None else iso(entry[4]),
545	                "recorded_at": iso(entry[5]),
546	            }
547	            for name, entry in sorted(projection.items())
548	        }
549	        return {
550	            "type": entity_type,
551	            "id": entity_id,
552	            "as_of": iso(as_of),
553	            "known_at": iso(known_at),
554	            "attributes": attributes,
555	        }
556	
557	    def _projection(
558	        self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str, as_of: int, known_at: int, required: bool = True
559	    ) -> Projection:
560	        row = self.store.entity_row(entity_type, entity_id)
561	        if row is None:
562	            raise NotFoundError(f"entity {entity_type}/{entity_id} does not exist")
563	        if int(row["created_at"]) > known_at:
564	            raise NotFoundError(
565	                f"entity {entity_type}/{entity_id} was not recorded yet at that transaction time"
